title: Symbol classes and real bundle pseudodifferential operators
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth positive volume form $dV$, and let $B,C$ be smooth finite-rank real vector bundles. Use the smooth-manifold, bundle, test-density and distribution conventions of [def-sfb-smooth-bundle-test-distributions]. Thus $\mathcal D'(B)$ is the continuous real-linear dual of compactly supported smooth $B^*\otimes|\Lambda^m T^*N|$ sections, with its strong dual topology. In a chart, a matrix symbol of integer order $r$ is a smooth function $a(x,\xi)$, with complex matrix entries, such that on every compact set of $x$ and for every pair of multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$ there is a finite constant $c_{\alpha\beta}$ satisfying $$\|\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\xi^\beta a(x,\xi)\|\leq c_{\alpha\beta}(1+|\xi|)^{r-|\beta|}.$$ Set $$\operatorname{Op}(a)f(x)=(2\pi)^{-m}\int e^{i(x-y)\cdot\xi}a(x,\xi)f(y)\,dy\,d\xi,$$ interpreted as an oscillatory integral: insert a smooth compactly supported frequency cutoff equal to one near zero, dilate its support to infinity, and take the limit after pairing with compactly supported smooth tests. On real inputs use the real part of this formula. For the localized terms below, transposition against tests is performed with both spatial cutoffs included: if $L_i=\chi_i\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(a_i)\psi_i$, then $(L_i u)(\phi)=u(L_i^t\phi)$, where $L_i^t$ is the transpose for the section–dual-density pairing. The input cutoff $\psi_i$ makes $L_i^t\phi$ compactly supported in $U_i$. A real pseudodifferential operator of order at most $r$, written $A\in\Psi^r(B,C)$, means a continuous real-linear map $\mathcal D'(B)\to\mathcal D'(C)$ admitting a finite representation $$A=\sum_i\chi_i\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(a_i)\psi_i+R_K.$$ Here the chart domains $U_i$ trivialize both bundles, $\chi_i,\psi_i\in C_c^\infty(U_i)$ act by multiplication, the $a_i$ are symbols of order $r$ in these frames, and the local inputs and outputs are extended by zero after the indicated cutoffs. The last term has a smooth kernel $K(x,y)\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf R}(B_y,C_x)$ on $N\times N$ and on smooth inputs is $$R_Ku(x)=\int_N K(x,y)u(y)\,dV(y),$$ with distributional action by duality in $y$. The empty sum is allowed in this definition. An operator with such a smooth kernel is called smoothing.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q43-50a30caf0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node def-sfb-smooth-bundle-test-distributions and the report in full, and diffed the item against its base text (from the Q21 run snapshot). There is no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply. A definition has no proof steps, so C1-C4 do not apply. The item changes in three ways. (1) D' is now cited from the new node and its topology is named as the strong dual, which is the usual topology on a compact N; this makes nothing easier. (2) The old sentence saying bare Op(a) acts on distributions by transposition is replaced by the transpose rule for chi_i Re Op(a_i) psi_i. I checked the counterexample: a=exp(-xi^2) gives a Gaussian whose transpose tails cannot be paired with u=exp(y^4). With cutoffs on both sides, L^t phi = psi Op^t(chi phi) has compact support in U_i. No hypothesis is added and no case dropped, and the report records the change under 'Statement corrected'. (3) stmt_deps gains only the new node. The rest of the statement is byte-identical to the base. The citers I read (Sobolev boundedness, parametrix) use only the cutoff representation, so neither changes meaning; the third citer (weak Garding) is the parent split. The new node is self-contained, with tests, seminorms, the strong dual, the smooth embedding, multiplication, chart derivatives and transposes. Edge cases hold: rank 0 gives D'=0, the circle gives classical D', and compactness means test sections need no support condition. It names the underlying notion of the definition as stage-1 section 3.2 asks, rather than restating it. rg -L over the DAG found no existing definition of bundle distributions; the other def-* hits are algebraic. The Mathlib searches cover all three kinds (Euclidean Distribution/TestFunction and ContMDiffSection do not match), so unsplit is right. The fields follow the rules and there is no SGA citation. Demailly's hodge-ams.pdf is not under literature/, so I could not check its page and equation numbers. The source field is inherited and unchanged, and the content is the standard S^r_{1,0} quantization.
